The particle and light objects of the framework are the following curves and
vector fields of the affine Minkowski model ([[def-sr-affine-minkowski-model]],
[[def-inertial-frame-and-inertial-chart]]), with the physical interpretation of
[[post-em-minkowski-physical-model]] and the units of

(a) [Worldlines] A **worldline** is a regular causal curve $x:J\to A$ in one of
the regularity classes of [[def-sr-regular-causal-curve-and-worldline]] ($J$ an
order-convex subset of $\mathbb R$ with at least two elements). A **massive
worldline** is a $C^k$ future timelike worldline, $k\ge1$, with everywhere
nonzero future timelike tangent; a **light ray** is a $C^1$ future null curve
with everywhere nonzero future null tangent. Along a null curve the integrand
$-\eta(x',x')$ of the proper-time construction
([[def-sr-proper-time]]) vanishes identically, so that construction yields no
proper-time parametrization of it, and a light ray is never treated as a
massive worldline. A worldline is a curve in spacetime; its reading $r\circ x$
in a named laboratory chart is a coordinate description of it, not an object of
another observer.

(b) [Four-velocity and four-acceleration] For a massive worldline the
four-velocity $U$ and, when it is $C^2$, the four-acceleration $A$ are those of
[[def-sr-four-velocity-and-four-acceleration]]; wherever defined they satisfy
$\eta(U,U)=-c^2$ and $\eta(U,A)=0$, by
[[thm-sr-proper-time-and-observer-decomposition]].

(c) [Chart reading] If a massive $C^2$ worldline is described in a laboratory
chart of [[def-em-lab-geometry]] by $t\mapsto(ct,r(t))$ on an open interval of
laboratory times, then $|r'(t)|<c$ for every $t$, with four-velocity
$U=\gamma(c,r')$ and Lorentz factor
$\gamma=(1-|r'|^2/c^2)^{-1/2}$, by clause (e) of
[[thm-sr-proper-time-and-observer-decomposition]].

(d) [Frames and observers] An inertial frame in this framework is the
origin-with-basis object of [[def-inertial-frame-and-inertial-chart]]; a point
observer is a future unit timelike vector $n\in V$ with rest space $n^\perp$ and
rest projection $h$, as in clauses (c)-(d) of
[[thm-sr-proper-time-and-observer-decomposition]]. An observer congruence and a
noninertial tetrad field are further objects, not defined by this item; the
words 'frame', 'chart', 'observer' and 'tetrad' denote distinct notions and are
not interchangeable.

Work in the oriented time-oriented affine Minkowski space $(A,V,\eta,C^+)$ ([[def-sr-affine-minkowski-model]]) with its inertial atlas ([[lem-affine-minkowski-charts-form-a-smooth-atlas]]) and the canonical identification of tangent spaces with $V$ ([[lem-tangent-space-of-affine-minkowski-space-is-v]]). The objects defined below are, in general, different objects, and the distinctions between them are part of the definition.

**(a) Chart and inertial chart.** A **chart** of the model is a diffeomorphism $u:U\to u(U)$ from a nonempty open subset $U\subseteq A$ onto an open subset of $\mathbb R^4$ ([[def-diffeomorphism-and-local-diffeomorphism-of-manifolds]], [[def-smooth-manifold]]), written with components $(u^0,u^1,u^2,u^3)$. An **inertial chart** is the global chart $x(p)=E^{-1}(p-o)$ of an inertial frame $(o;e_0,e_1,e_2,e_3)$ ([[def-inertial-frame-and-inertial-chart]]). A general chart need not be inertial: if $x$ is an inertial chart and $N:x(U)\to\mathbb R^4$ is a diffeomorphism onto its image which is not the restriction of an affine map, then $u:=N\circ x$ is a chart that is not inertial, because if $u$ were the inertial chart of a frame then $x\circ u^{-1}=N^{-1}$ would be affine by [[lem-inertial-chart-transitions-are-affine-lorentz]] and hence $N=(N^{-1})^{-1}$ would be affine as the inverse of an affine bijection, a contradiction; the map $N(y)=(y^0,y^1+(y^0)^2,y^2,y^3)$ on $\mathbb R^4$ is an explicit example.

**(b) Tetrad at an event and tetrad field.** A **tetrad at $p\in A$** is an ordered basis $(e_0,e_1,e_2,e_3)$ of $V$ with $\eta(e_a,e_b)=\operatorname{diag}(-1,1,1,1)_{ab}$ and $e_0$ future, $e_0\in C^+$ ([[def-causal-classification-of-lorentz-vectors]], [[def-time-orientation-and-future-causal-sets]]): this is the basis of an inertial frame without an origin and without the orientation condition. A **tetrad field** on a nonempty open subset $\Omega\subseteq A$ is a tuple $(E_0,E_1,E_2,E_3)$ of smooth vector fields on $\Omega$ ([[def-ck-tensor-field-on-minkowski-space]], type $(1,0)$) whose values at every $p\in\Omega$ form a tetrad at $p$. A tetrad field is **observer-adapted** to a prescribed future timelike worldline or congruence when $E_0=U/c$ for the corresponding future timelike unit vector field $U$ with $\eta(U,U)=-c^2$ ([[def-sr-regular-causal-curve-and-worldline]]).

**(c) Observer congruence.** An **observer congruence** on a nonempty open subset $\Omega\subseteq A$ is a smooth vector field $n:\Omega\to V$ with $\eta(n,n)=-1$ and $n(p)\in C^+$ for every $p\in\Omega$. Its **observers** are its maximal integral curves ([[def-integral-curve-of-a-vector-field]], [[thm-unique-maximal-integral-curve-through-each-point]]). Each observer is a future timelike worldline ([[def-sr-regular-causal-curve-and-worldline]]): its tangent at a parameter value $s$ is $n(x(s))$, which is future timelike, and it is regular because $\eta(n,n)=-1$ makes $n$ nowhere zero. **Completeness** of the integral curves, a global product structure of $\Omega$, and global synchronization are not asserted by this definition.

- **Non-inertial charts exist, and the example is checked.** The map $N(y)=(y^0,y^1+(y^0)^2,y^2,y^3)$ is a diffeomorphism of $\mathbb R^4$ with the smooth two-sided inverse $z\mapsto(z^0,z^1-(z^0)^2,z^2,z^3)$. It is not the restriction of an affine map: $N(0)=0$ and $N(2e_0)=(2,4,0,0)\ne2N(e_0)=(2,2,0,0)$ for $e_0=(1,0,0,0)$, so $N$ is not linear, and with $N(0)=0$ it is therefore not affine. If $N\circ x$ were an inertial chart, the transition $x\circ(N\circ x)^{-1}=N^{-1}$ between inertial charts would be affine by [[lem-inertial-chart-transitions-are-affine-lorentz]]; the inverse of an affine bijection $z\mapsto Az+b$ of $\mathbb R^4$ is again affine, $w\mapsto A^{-1}w-A^{-1}b$ ([[def-lorentz-map-and-lorentz-group]]), so $N$ would be affine, a contradiction. Hence $N\circ x$ is a chart that is not inertial, and being $C^\infty$ it belongs to the model's smooth structure.

this limit, written $x'(s) \in V$, is the **tangent vector** of $x$ at $s$, and

A **future timelike worldline** (equivalently, a **massive worldline**) is a
$C^{1}$ curve $x : I \to A$ with $x'(s)$ future timelike for every $s \in I$; a
**future causal curve** (respectively a **future null curve**) is a $C^{1}$
curve with $x'(s)$ future causal (respectively future null) for every
$s \in I$. A **piecewise $C^{1}$ worldline** is a piecewise $C^{1}$ curve whose
tangents at every point of each open smooth piece and whose finite one-sided
difference-quotient tangents at both endpoints of every piece are future
timelike; a **$C^{k}$ worldline** is a worldline whose parametrization is
$C^{k}$. $C^{2}$ regularity is what makes the four-acceleration of
[[def-sr-four-velocity-and-four-acceleration]] available.

- **Well-definedness.** The difference quotient is an element of $V$ because
the affine action assigns a displacement to every ordered pair of events. The
limit in $V$ is taken in the transported Euclidean norm $|v|_{E} = |E^{-1}v|_{2}$
of an inertial frame isomorphism $E$, and the choice of frame does not matter:
for inertial frames $E$ and $E'$ the maps $E'^{-1}E$ and its inverse are
Euclidean linear maps, so by
[[lem-euclidean-linear-maps-have-matrices-and-are-bounded]] they are bounded
with constants $K, K' \ge 0$, which gives
$|v|_{E'} \le K'|v|_{E}$ and $|v|_{E} \le K|v|_{E'}$ on $V$; equivalent norms
have the same convergent sequences and the same limits, and hence the same
derivative $x'(s)$. The identification with the coordinate calculus, the value
$x'(s) = E\bigl((x_A \circ x)'(s)\bigr)$, the independence of the class $C^{k}$
and the continuity of $x'$ are then read through the same linear isomorphism,
with the published vector-valued derivative and continuity of
[[def-vector-valued-derivative-and-integral]] and
[[def-vector-valued-functions-limits-and-continuity]] as the coordinate
calculus, and the one-sided endpoint derivatives are the one-sided limits over
the domain $I$ used by that same definition. The affine chart transitions of
[[lem-affine-minkowski-charts-form-a-smooth-atlas]] are consistent with this
dictionary: they are affine with an invertible linear part, so they compose the
coordinate calculus with a bounded linear change of coordinates.
- **Regularity is implicit in every causal character.** Because the zero vector
is excluded from timelike, null and spacelike alike
([[def-causal-classification-of-lorentz-vectors]]), the future timelike
condition $x'(s) \in C^{+}$ already contains $x'(s) \ne 0$, and each side of a
corner in the piecewise clause is required to carry a nonzero future timelike
one-sided tangent. Null and spacelike curves are distinguished from massive
worldlines and are used later only to delimit the proper-time construction,
which is stated for future timelike worldlines alone.
- **No choice principle is used.** All objects are finite-dimensional or
explicitly parametrized; the definition selects nothing from a family.

Adopt as physical assumptions of this framework, extending the ideal-clock

calculus of this page:

interaction (a **free particle**) has as its worldline a straight future
timelike line of the affine model ([[def-sr-affine-minkowski-model]]): there are
an event $p \in A$ and a future timelike vector $v \in V$ with
$x(s) = p + (s-s_0)v$ for all $s$ ([[def-sr-regular-causal-curve-and-worldline]]).
Interactions, forces and collisions are not part of this assumption: a particle
that is not free may have any future timelike worldline admitted by its own
dynamical model, and no force law is adopted here. The kinematical consequences
of this shape for the four-velocity are derived, not assumed, in
[[pthm-sr-four-velocity-norm-and-orthogonality]].

**(ii) Clock hypothesis.** An ideal clock carried along a future timelike
worldline of the model, including an accelerated one and a piecewise $C^{1}$ one
with finitely many kinks, reads between any two parameter values the proper-time
difference of [[def-sr-proper-time]] for $C^{1}$ histories and of
[[def-sr-piecewise-proper-time]] for weak piecewise $C^{1}$ histories, with no
additional term depending on acceleration, jerk or any higher derivative. A
kink is an idealization of a finite short acceleration phase whose contribution
is included through the integral on the smooth pieces, and the reading does not
depend on an increasing regular change of parameter admitted by the curve
definition — its derivatives on smooth pieces and all finite one-sided endpoint
derivatives are positive, as in
[[lem-sr-proper-time-reparametrization-invariance]] and
[[lem-sr-piecewise-proper-time-reparametrization-invariance]]. Zero-tangent
compositions are not worldlines of this model.

**(iii) Scope and qualification.** The assumptions concern ideal point
particles, ideal clocks and flat classical spacetime. They are adopted, not
proved; they are not consequences of the affine geometry, and no experiment is
claimed here to establish them. They inherit the idealizations of
[[post-sr-ideal-clocks-and-light]]: real clocks have finite resolution,
calibration and apparatus limitations, and real particles are not exactly free.
The coordinate and unit conventions are those of
[[def-sr-si-units-and-coordinate-conventions]], and inertial charts are those
of [[def-inertial-frame-and-inertial-chart]].

(a) (Box identity.) For each $b$, with $F_a^+:=\{x\in B:x^a=d_a\}$, $F_a^-:=\{x\in B:x^a=c_a\}$ and each face integral the Riemann integral over the remaining three coordinates, $$\int_B f^b\,d^4x=\sum_{a=0}^{3}\Big(\int_{F_a^+}T^{ab}\,d^3x-\int_{F_a^-}T^{ab}\,d^3x\Big).$$ (b) (Slice balance.) Write $K:=\prod_{i=1}^{3}[c_i,d_i]$ and, for $s\in[c_0,d_0]$, $Q^b(s):=\int_K T^{0b}(s,x)\,d^3x$; this is finite and continuous in $s$. For $c_0\le s_1<s_2\le d_0$, $$Q^b(s_2)-Q^b(s_1)=\int_{[s_1,s_2]\times K} f^b\,d^4x-\sum_{i=1}^{3}\Big(\int_{[s_1,s_2]\times K_i^+}T^{ib}\,d^3x-\int_{[s_1,s_2]\times K_i^-}T^{ib}\,d^3x\Big),$$ where $K_i^\pm$ are the two faces $x^i=d_i$, $x^i=c_i$ of $K$. (c) (Finite-flux conservation.) If $f=0$ on $[s_1,s_2]\times K$ and $T^{ib}=0$ on the side faces $[s_1,s_2]\times K_i^\pm$ for $i=1,2,3$, then $Q^b(s_1)=Q^b(s_2)$ for every $b$. The theorem concerns finite axis-parallel boxes in one inertial chart and is proved by the fundamental theorem of calculus. It does not assert a flux identity for arbitrary regions or hypersurfaces, does not assert that $Q^b$ transforms as a four-vector under a change of inertial chart, and asserts no conservation without the stated side-flux hypothesis; no noncompact or limiting statement is made. Adopt as physical assumptions of this framework, extending [[post-sr-ideal-clocks-and-light]] (ideal vacuum light rays are exactly the future null straight lines, with coordinate speed $c$ in every inertial chart) and [[post-sr-inertial-covariance]] (the affine Minkowski model, with the model's equations covariant under proper orthochronous affine Lorentz maps):

**(i) Ideal plane wave.** An ideal monochromatic light wave in vacuum is modeled, in any inertial chart, by a dimensionless affine phase $\theta$ with future null wave covector $k$ ([[def-sr-affine-phase-and-wave-covector]], [[lem-sr-null-covector-frame-data]]): the level sets of $\theta$ are the wave fronts, every line $p+\mathbb Rk^\sharp$ has constant phase, and the rays of this ideal wave are the future null straight lines $p+\mathbb R_{\ge0}k^\sharp$, consistently with the general ideal-light clause that the ideal vacuum light rays are exactly the future null straight lines. The model is one ideal plane wave: constant wave covector, no medium, no dispersion, no absorption, no modulation or envelope, no boundary or source model, no intensity or polarization model.

**(ii) Frequency reading.** An ideal observer of the model with four-velocity $U_o=cn$ ($n$ future unit timelike) that receives this wave reads the angular frequency $\omega_n:=-ck(n)=-k(U_o)$ and the linear frequency $\omega_n/(2\pi)$ of [[def-sr-null-wave-covector-and-observer-frequency]], that is, minus the rate of change of the phase with respect to the observer's own proper time with the sign convention that this number is positive ([[lem-sr-phase-rate-along-worldline]], [[lem-sr-future-causal-pairing-negative]]). The reading is attached to the observer's worldline at the event of reception.

**(iv) Scope and exclusions.** These are adopted idealizations, not deductions from experiment and not claims about nature. No quantum photon model and no identification of energy with $\hbar\omega$ is made (excluded by the conventions of [[def-sr-si-units-and-coordinate-conventions]]); no claim is made that real light, real clocks, real receivers or real sources are exactly described; dispersive, absorbing, nonlinear or modulated media, finite line width, intensity, polarization, source and detector physics, gravitation, quantum effects and accelerated-observer reception are outside the model. Empirical tests of the model belong to the framework's experimental work and are not asserted here.

Adopt as a separate model premise for ideal massless particles, independent of
[[post-sr-massive-particle-dynamics]] whose formula $P=mU$ uses $m>0$ and does
not define a massless case:

**(i) The object.** An ideal massless particle of the model is described by a
nonzero future null vector $P\in V$
([[def-causal-classification-of-lorentz-vectors]],
[[def-time-orientation-and-future-causal-sets]]) whose SI unit is kilogram
metre per second ([[def-sr-si-units-and-coordinate-conventions]]). Such a $P$
is not of the form $mU$ for any $m>0$ and any future timelike $U$ with
$\eta(U,U)=-c^2$: a positive multiple of a timelike vector is timelike, and
the zero vector is neither timelike, null nor spacelike, so the massive
formula $P=mU$ of [[def-sr-four-velocity-and-four-acceleration]] degenerates
to $0$ at $m=0$ and does not describe a nonzero null momentum. The particle
therefore has no four-velocity, no proper-time parametrisation and no rest
frame. Its scale is fixed by a measured energy in an observer's frame.

**(ii) Observer identification.** Relative to a future unit observer $n$, the
model identifies the measured energy and spatial momentum of the particle with
the quantities $E_n(P)=-c\,\eta(P,n)$ and $q_n(P)=h(P)$ of
[[def-sr-observed-energy-momentum-and-kinetic-energy]]. Necessarily
$E_n(P)=c\,|q_n(P)|>0$, by
[[lem-sr-energy-momentum-observer-identities]]\,(a)(i), and no rest mass, rest
energy or kinetic energy is assigned to the particle — the definition of
$T_n$ requires a rest-mass parameter $m$ and no such parameter is introduced
here. This clause is a formulation convention identifying mathematical
quantities with the quantities the model calls measured; it is not a
measurement report and no experiment is claimed.

Adopt as physical assumptions of the relativistic particle model, on top of the
flat spacetime model of [[def-sr-affine-minkowski-model]] and the SI unit
conventions of [[def-sr-si-units-and-coordinate-conventions]], together with
the framework's idealisations of point particles, ideal clocks and ideal light
signals:

**(i) Mass and momentum.** Every massive classical particle of the model
carries a positive constant invariant mass parameter $m>0$ and has
four-momentum $P=mU$, where $U$ is the four-velocity of its future timelike
worldline ([[def-sr-regular-causal-curve-and-worldline]],
[[def-sr-four-velocity-and-four-acceleration]],
[[thm-sr-proper-time-and-observer-decomposition]]); $P$ is a vector of $V$
whose SI unit is kilogram metre per second. The formula is adopted only for
$m>0$; the case $m=0$ is not defined by it and is the separate premise
[[post-sr-ideal-massless-particle-momentum]]. In particular $\eta(P,P)=-m^2c^2$
is a consequence of the four-velocity normalisation, not a separate
assumption.

**(ii) Observer measurement identification.** Relative to a future unit
observer $n$, the model identifies the measured energy of the particle with
$E_n(P)$, its measured spatial momentum with $q_n(P)$, its kinetic energy with
$T_n(P)=E_n(P)-mc^2$ and its rest energy with $mc^2$, where $E_n,q_n,T_n$ are
the quantities of [[def-sr-observed-energy-momentum-and-kinetic-energy]]; the
units are the joule, kilogram metre per second and kilogram of
[[def-sr-si-units-and-coordinate-conventions]]. This clause is a formulation
convention identifying mathematical quantities with the quantities the model
calls measured; it is not a measurement report and no experiment is claimed.

**(iii) Isolated collision balance.** In an isolated collision of particles at
an event — the interaction being confined to that event, with no external
agent acting — the sum of the incoming four-momenta equals the sum of the
outgoing four-momenta, in the sense of the collision data of
[[def-sr-collision-datum-and-conservation]]: the model adopts
$Q_{\mathrm{in}}=Q_{\mathrm{out}}$ for such an isolated datum. No particular
collision is asserted to occur, and no mechanism, probability, cross section
or amplitude is supplied by this clause.

**(iv) Equation of motion for a stipulated force.** Whenever an interaction is
described by a stipulated force law $F$, that is a map assigning to an event
and a future timelike four-velocity a vector of $V$ on a stated domain, the
model's particle equation is $m\,dU/d\tau=F(x,U)$ along the worldline, with
$dU/d\tau$ the proper-time derivative of
[[def-sr-proper-time-derivative-and-four-force]], so that the stipulated $F$
is the four-force of the motion. A particular force law, and the existence,
uniqueness and domain of solutions of the resulting equation, are not adopted
here and belong to a separate model.

[[def-sr-si-units-and-coordinate-conventions]]. It proves nothing new; it

In the model the reading of an ideal clock between two events of its history is
the proper-time integral of its worldline, by clause (i) of
[[post-sr-ideal-clocks-and-light]] for $C^1$ histories and by clause (ii) of
[[post-sr-free-trajectories-and-clock-hypothesis]] for the weak piecewise $C^1$
class ([[def-sr-piecewise-proper-time]]); no term depending on the
four-acceleration ([[def-sr-four-velocity-and-four-acceleration]]) or on any
higher derivative of the history appears, and the clock hypothesis is precisely
the exclusion of such terms. The corner of the piecewise inertial history is an
idealization: a physical turnaround occupies a finite parameter interval, the
worldline is then $C^1$ or smooth there, and its proper time is still the
integral. The endpoint bound and strictness clause of
[[thm-sr-endpoint-proper-time-bound-and-flat-maximum]] apply to every weak
piecewise history, so the comparison with the stay-at-home clock survives the
smoothing of the corner, and the strict inequality remains because a smoothed
itinerary still does not have the image of the straight segment.

One history of the reunion is the straight segment from $p$ to $q$; the other
contains the corner event $r$ of [[texp-sr-piecewise-inertial-twin-reunion]], and
the three events $p,r,q$ are not collinear: in the chart of that item their
coordinate columns are $(0,0,0,0)$, $(cT,vT,0,0)$ and $(2cT,0,0,0)$ with
$vT\ne0$. Every change of inertial chart is an affine bijection
([[lem-inertial-chart-transitions-are-affine-lorentz]]) and maps collinear
triples to collinear triples, so no change of inertial frame maps the image of
the stay-at-home history onto the image of the traveler's history, nor fixes both
endpoints and exchanges the two histories. The two twins are therefore not
related by an inertial change of description, and the difference of readings is
a model consequence of the different histories, not a consequence of who is
'really moving': the symmetric time-dilation relation of
[[lem-sr-boost-time-length-and-velocity-formulas]] (i) concerns the two frames,
while the reunion comparison concerns the two clock readings at the single
common event $q$.

In each momentary inertial rest frame of the traveler the stay-at-home clock runs
slow by the factor $1/\gamma$, and the traveler may legitimately apply the
time-dilation relation between events that are simultaneous in that momentary
frame ([[lem-sr-boost-time-length-and-velocity-formulas]] (i),
[[def-sr-simultaneity-slice-and-rest-distance]]). But the two legs use different
inertial frames. With $\gamma=(1-v^2/c^2)^{-1/2}$ and the turn event $r$ of
[[texp-sr-piecewise-inertial-twin-reunion]], the outbound rest frame's chart
$x'$ satisfies $x'^0=\gamma\bigl(x^0-\frac vc x^1\bigr)$, so its slice through
$r$ has $x'^0=\gamma cT(1-v^2/c^2)=cT/\gamma$ and meets the stay-at-home
worldline $x^1=0$ at $x^0=\frac{1}{\gamma}\cdot\frac{cT}{\gamma}=cT(1-v^2/c^2)$,
that is at coordinate time $t=T(1-v^2/c^2)=T/\gamma^2$; the inbound rest frame's
chart $x''$ satisfies $x''^0=\gamma\bigl(x^0+\frac vc x^1\bigr)$, and its slice
through $r$ meets the same worldline at $x^0=cT(1+v^2/c^2)$, that is at
coordinate time $t=T(1+v^2/c^2)$. The two slices differ by
$2Tv^2/c^2$ in coordinate time, and the identity
$$2T=\frac{T}{\gamma^2}+\frac{2Tv^2}{c^2}+\frac{T}{\gamma^2},$$
which only uses $1/\gamma^2=1-v^2/c^2$, inserts this gap into the traveler's two
leg-by-leg accounts and reproduces the stay-at-home reading $2T$ at the reunion,
in agreement with the conditional comparison result
[[pthm-sr-same-endpoint-clock-comparison]]. The naive reciprocity statement
'each twin judges the other's clock to run slow' therefore compares different
pairs of events for the two travelers — events simultaneous in different
momentary frames — and does not apply to the reunion comparison, which concerns
the two clock readings at the single common event $q$.

Adopt as physical assumptions of the special-relativity framework the following
two statements, with the SI coordinate and unit conventions of
[[def-sr-si-units-and-coordinate-conventions]].

- **Adopted, not proved.** Both clauses are adopted assumptions of the
  framework, with the physical interpretation fixed by

- **Ideal apparatus, complete vacuum, geometric ray regime.** The light clause
  concerns ideal light in complete vacuum in the geometric (nondispersive) ray
  regime. No dispersive or refractive medium is described, and the ray model
  carries no wave-optics, coherence or intensity structure.
- **No quantum photon model.** No photon is assumed, and in particular the
  frequency of the ideal light is not identified with an energy by a factor
  $\hbar$ anywhere in this framework's primitive layer.
- **Later development.** Parametrization invariance of the clock reading, the
  proper-time function along general worldlines, four-velocity and
  four-acceleration are developed on the later worldlines-and-clocks page from
  its own items; the present item states the reading rule and the ray
  interpretation for the model and does not derive that theory here.
- **Empirical status.** Agreement of an experiment with predictions of this
  model would be evidence about the specified model and its auxiliary
  assumptions; it would not be a proof of this postulate, and a finite dataset
  cannot establish its exact validity.

**(i) Total tensor.** In every conservation or integration statement of this framework the tensor used is the total stress-energy tensor of the system considered, including every constituent that carries energy-momentum — matter, fields and supporting structures present in the region — assembled by the additivity clause of [[post-sr-matter-models-and-evolution]].

**(ii) Localisation.** Whenever conservation of a slice four-momentum over a coordinate-time interval $[s_1,s_2]$ is asserted in an inertial chart, the model assumes that during that interval the total tensor is $C^1$ and symmetric on a neighbourhood of a closed box $[s_1,s_2]\times\bar K$ ([[def-sr-stress-energy-tensor-and-force-density]], [[def-sr-affine-minkowski-model]]), that its components satisfy the zero side-flux condition $T^{ib}=0$ on the spatial faces of the box for $i=1,2,3$, and that the slice integrals converge; equivalently, the system is isolated inside the chosen region for the chosen interval.

**(iii) Failure of isolation.** If the side flux does not vanish, only the exact finite-flux balance of [[thm-sr-stress-balance-and-finite-flux]] is asserted; no conservation of a slice integral is inferred and no limiting procedure at spatial infinity is adopted.

**(iv) Unmodelled matter.** For a matter system not governed by one of the models of [[post-sr-matter-models-and-evolution]], conservation of its stress-energy tensor is not inferred; if used it must be adopted or derived separately.

The force vocabulary of this framework has two distinct mathematical carriers. On a massive particle worldline the four-force is $F=\dot P=dP/d\tau$ ([[def-sr-proper-time-derivative-and-four-force]]), and its identities are conditional on the adopted particle dynamics [[post-sr-massive-particle-dynamics]]. In the continuum the force carrier is the four-force density $f^b=\partial_aT^{ab}$ of a symmetric type-$(2,0)$ field ([[def-sr-stress-energy-tensor-and-force-density]]). Neither object is a force law: the definition of $\dot P$ asserts no equation of motion, and the definition of $f$ asserts no conservation and no interaction.

The page's conservation statements are conditional deductions. Local conservation of the scalar, dust and fluid tensors is proved from the adopted model equations of [[pthm-sr-local-stress-energy-conservation]]; for any other matter the conservation of $T$ must be adopted or derived separately, and no conservation is asserted for an arbitrary prescribed symmetric field. Integrated conservation additionally requires the isolation premise of [[post-sr-matter-isolation-and-total-stress-energy]] and is asserted only for finite boxes and slices in one inertial chart [[pthm-sr-integrated-conservation-for-isolated-matter]]; it does not supply a four-vector transformation law for the slice integrals and does not extend to noncompact regions.
